Brown Soda Bread with Salted Butter

Served at: Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid)

Serves 8Prep 15 minCook 35 min

Brown Soda Bread is a traditional Irish bread made with baking soda instead of yeast, giving it a dense, hearty texture. It is often served during the Feast of St. Muirgen, also known as Lí Ban the Mermaid, as a comforting staple that honors Irish heritage and the coastal origins of the legend. Paired with salted butter, it highlights the simple, rustic flavors cherished during this celebration.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) whole wheat flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 3/4 cups (420 ml) buttermilk
  • Salted butter, for serving

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, baking soda, and salt.
  3. Make a well in the center and gradually pour in the buttermilk, mixing with a wooden spoon until a sticky dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough onto a floured surface and gently knead it just until it comes together into a round loaf, about 1-2 minutes; do not over-knead.
  5. Place the dough on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  6. Using a sharp knife, cut a deep cross on top of the dough to help it cook evenly.
  7. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the bread is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
  8. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before slicing.
  9. Serve warm with salted butter spread generously on each slice.

Tips

  • Use fresh buttermilk for the best rise and flavor.
  • For a softer crust, wrap the bread in a clean towel as it cools.
  • Add a tablespoon of rolled oats on top before baking for a rustic finish.
